topSignals.title: Priority stacks Elcogen and Topsoe remain quiet — 31 and 56 days respectively since their last SOFC/SOEC-specific company news.
topSignals.text: Direct fetches of both newsrooms today confirm no new solid-oxide item: Elcogen's News & Insights feed still tops out at the Oct 6 "Insights" electrification thought-piece (already logged, not product/company news), behind which sit the already-logged Sept 23 SOEC whitepaper and Sept 21 Metrosert testing-cooperation announcement — so the last genuine News-category item is still Sept 21 (31 days). Topsoe's press-releases page remains topped by the Oct 14 Bharat Petroleum SAF hydrotreating contract (hydroprocessing business, out of SOFC/SOEC scope); the last SOFC/SOEC-relevant Topsoe release is still the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset (56 days). items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new News-category item since Sept 21 (Metrosert testing cooperation); the Oct 6 Insights thought-piece and Sept 23 SOEC whitepaper are both already logged. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC, vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release; topsoe.com/press-releases is topped by the Oct 14 Bharat Petroleum SAF contract (hydroprocessing, out of scope). Last SOFC/SOEC-relevant release remains the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset (56 days).

Today's dedicated rotation — cycle 3, round 4 (Huatsing Power, Ningbo SOFCMAN, Chaozhou Three-Circle/CCTC, Nexceris, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura), 7-day lookback: No new items for any of the six.

Huatsing Power: No English- or Chinese-language company/product news; results were academic SOFC/SOEC review papers and generic market-landscape pages that mention the company only as a listed participant. Open coverage gap, consistent with prior rotations.
Ningbo SOFCMAN: Same pattern — Chinese Academy of Sciences archive pages, generic market reports, and academic citations; no 2026-dated company disclosure found.

Chaozhou Three-Circle (CCTC): Fourth dedicated search in this monitor; again no company-specific SOFC/SOEC news in English or Chinese, only its Wikipedia profile and generic market-report listings (GII). Standing data gap.
Nexceris: Results were the already-logged $60M SOEC-scaling deal and LEVER-process materials (2024/2025-vintage); no new 2026 item.
Kawasaki Heavy Industries: Results were SOFC market-research report listings and a 2024-dated Symbio fuel-cell-systems MoU (already background); no new company-specific SOFC disclosure.
Miura: Results were the already-logged Miura/Ceres 4.2kW SOFC CHP launch and maintenance-network items (2020-2024 vintage); no new 2026 milestone.

Sweep 1 — "Bloom Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR FuelCell Energy": No new items; results were recycled coverage of the Ceres-Weichai licensing deal, the Goldman Sachs Ceres upgrade, and a 2016-vintage Cummins/Ceres DOE data-center fuel-cell story (confirmed via direct fetch, not new — same false-positive previously logged on Oct 11).

Sweep 2 — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell": No new items; results were the already-logged Sept 18 Doosan-Reverion $78M/€60M SOFC stack supply contract, recirculated across several outlets.

Other key players (Bloom Energy, Ceres Power, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Doosan Fuel Cell, SK ecoplant, Weichai, Kyocera, Aisin, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol, Plansee, Watt Fuel Cell, OxEon Energy): not in today's dedicated rotation; no items surfaced incidentally beyond what is already logged.

Watch item, not a benchmark entry: SFA, a South Korean industrial-equipment manufacturer, surfaced in a secondary-source (enkiai.com) article describing a "picks-and-shovels" strategy supplying fuel-cell manufacturing equipment, with two inconsistent Chinese order figures (~$224M / ~$204M, April 2026) and an unverified, unattributed claim of "$7.65B in binding agreements to power AI data centers" in a 90-day period. SFA makes equipment, not SOFC stacks/systems itself, and the figures are not sourced to primary disclosures — not added to the benchmark register, flagged for a primary-source follow-up only.
